title: Azure Regions and Availability Zones
description: Understand Azure regions, availability zones, and geographies so you can choose the right location for your cloud resources.

data.text: When you create an Azure resource, you choose a **region** — a geographic location where Azure runs its data centers. The region you choose affects speed, cost, compliance, and availability.
Azure arranges its infrastructure in a hierarchy: **geographies** contain **regions**, and regions contain **availability zones**. Understanding this hierarchy helps you build reliable applications.

data.caption: Azure's geographic infrastructure hierarchy
data.definition:
flowchart TD
    A[Geography: North Europe] --> B[Region: UK South]
    A --> C[Region: UK West]
    B --> D[Availability Zone 1]
    B --> E[Availability Zone 2]
    B --> F[Availability Zone 3]
    G[Geography: West Europe] --> H[Region: North Europe]
    G --> I[Region: West Europe]

data.title: Definitions
items: **Geography** — a discrete market, usually a country or group of countries, that preserves data-residency and compliance boundaries
**Region** — an area within a geography containing one or more data centers
**Availability zone** — physically separate locations within a region to protect against data center failures

data.text: Choosing the right region is one of the first decisions you make in Azure. Here are the main factors to consider.

rows: Choose a region close to your users for faster response times
Some data must stay in specific countries or regions
Not all services are available in every region
Use multiple regions for disaster recovery

data.text: Availability zones are physically separate locations within a region, each with independent power, cooling, and networking. When you deploy resources across multiple zones, Azure ensures that a failure in one zone does not take down your entire application.

terms.definition: A geographic area containing one or more Azure data centers.
A physically isolated location within an Azure region for high availability.
A market area (usually a country or region) used for data-residency and compliance.
The time it takes for data to travel from your users to Azure's data centers.

data.title: Specifying a Region in Azure CLI
data.code:
# Create a resource group in the West Europe region
az group create \
  --name myResourceGroup \
  --location westeurope

# List all available regions
az account list-locations --output table

data.title: Key Takeaways
points: Geographies define compliance and data-residency boundaries
Regions are groups of data centers within a geography
Availability zones protect against data center failures within a region
Choose regions close to your users for low latency
Not all Azure services are available in every region
data.takeaway: The region you choose affects performance, compliance, and reliability. Always plan for high availability by using availability zones when possible.
